Frequently Asked Questions

How do you decide between repairing and replacing a system in an older Piedmont home?

By documented condition, not age alone. The diagnostic establishes what failed and what the rest of the unit looks like, then repair and replacement get priced side by side. A sound older system with one bad component is a repair; a failing compressor on a unit near end of life usually is not.

Why does my water pressure drop only when two fixtures run at once?

That pattern points to restricted supply rather than a fixture problem, commonly a partially closed or failing valve, undersized lines, or buildup narrowing older pipe. A pressure assessment measures static and flowing pressure to isolate the restriction, and the repair gets quoted from the measurement.

Is an air scrubber different from just buying better filters?

Yes, they work differently and cover different things. A filter captures particles passing through it on the return side; an in-duct scrubber treats air continuously as it moves, reaching finer particles and operating on every cycle. Many homes run both, with the filter matched to the blower so airflow does not suffer.

Can a generator power my well pump and HVAC together during an outage?

With correct sizing, yes. Pumps and compressors draw hard at startup, so the load calculation accounts for surge demand, not just running watts. The estimate prices a unit sized for those loads together and a smaller essential-circuits option, so the trade-off is visible.

Which communities near Piedmont do you serve?

Powdersville, Pelzer, and Easley all fall inside standard coverage, and the chat team can confirm any address on the county line in minutes.
